extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians organizing or presenting talks at AMS meetings (organizers, authors submitting abstracts, and presenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and formatting guidelines for presenters, organizers, and abstract submitters for AMS meetings: deadlines, program numbering, speaker symbols, time limits, and abstract ordering/classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaker-symbol legend and role indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Symbols indicate speaker roles: • AMS Invited Lecturer; * Special Session Speaker; ... Graduate Student; ... Undergraduate Student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the designated symbols next to names to communicate speaker type/role on the program; this legend appears at the start of presenter listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-position numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers following the name indicate the speaker's position on the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The parenthetical numbers after listings correspond to positions used to order abstracts in the Abstracts volume (see abstract-ordering rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for contributed papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit for each contributed paper in the sessions is ten minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speakers should prepare talks to fit the ten-minute contributed-paper slot; this is a general rule for sessions (special sessions may differ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-sessions time limits and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Special Sessions the time limit varies from session to session and within sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To maintain the schedule, time limits will be strictly enforced. Presenters in special sessions must check their specific session's allotted time and adhere strictly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presenter identification for multi-author papers
rubrics_metrics.description: For papers with more than one author, an asterisk follows the name of the author who plans to present the paper at the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When listing authors on the program, mark with an asterisk the individual who will actually present so program readers and organizers know the presenter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undergraduate-interest flagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers flagged with a solid triangle (▸) have been designated by the author as being of possible interest to undergraduate students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may mark their abstracts/papers to indicate likely undergraduate interest; the program will display this flag so students and instructors can identify suitable talks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts ordering and numbering convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts of papers presented in the sessions will be found in the Abstracts volume, ordered according to the numbers in parentheses following the listings. The middle two digits (e.g., 897-20-1136) refer to the Mathematical Reviews subject classification assigned by the individual author. Groups of papers for each subject are listed chronologically in the Abstracts. The last one to four digits refer to the receipt number of the abstract; abstracts are further sorted by the receipt number within each classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting an abstract, authors supply a Math Reviews subject classification; abstracts are grouped by that classification and then by receipt number, which determines ordering in the Abstracts publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines for organizers, special-session contributions, abstracts, and summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Each meeting listing includes deadlines for organizers, for consideration of contributed papers in special sessions, for abstracts, and sometimes for summaries to MAA organizers (dates vary by meeting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers and authors must meet the listed deadlines (which may be listed as specific dates, 'Expired', or 'To be announced') for inclusion in announcement/program issues and the Abstracts volume; deadlines differ by meeting and must be checked per meeting announcement.
